_comment: One description of this standalone lesson build, read by every tool in ../lesson-app-tools/. Order here IS the teaching order and IS the unit number: unit N is lessons[N-1]. NOTE this build differs from grade-1-app and grade-2-app in one way that matters to any tool that patches a lesson: these .html files are GENERATED from src/ by src/build-all.sh, so a patch applied to them alone is discarded by the next rebuild. Wiring belongs in the fragments.
subject: mathematics

lessons.title: Up to a Thousand
lessons.materials: A place-value chart or three columns marked hundreds, tens and ones, and about a hundred small things to group into piles of ten. Building a three-digit number out of real hundreds, tens and ones is what makes the columns mean something.
lessons.atHome: Find three-digit numbers around you, on a house, a bus or a price tag. Say how many hundreds, tens and ones each one has, and put three of them in order from smallest to largest.

warmUp.q: Let's warm up. In Grade 2 you worked with tens and ones. How many tens are there in 60?
warmUp.why: 60 is 6 tens. Today you will go past 100, into the hundreds.

lessons.title: Adding, Taking Away and Money
lessons.materials: A handful of real coins and notes, or play money, up to 1000 shillings, and a hundred square or number line for the sums. Counting out change and crossing a hundred when you add is worth doing with real money before it is done on a page.
lessons.atHome: Make a pretend shop with prices under 500 shillings. Add two prices together, then work out the change from a 1000-shilling note by counting on.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you worked with numbers up to a thousand. Warm up: what is 300 add 200?
warmUp.why: 3 hundreds and 2 hundreds make 5 hundreds, which is 500. Today you will add, take away and work with money.

lessons.title: Rows and Rules
lessons.materials: Bottle tops, buttons or counters to lay out in equal rows, and about 13 small things to share into groups of 4. An array you build yourself is what turns a times table from something recited into something seen.
lessons.atHome: Lay out bottle tops or buttons in rows to make arrays: 3 rows of 4 is 12, and so is 4 rows of 3. Say one times table aloud on the way to school, then share 13 beans into groups of 4 and see what is left over.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you added and worked with money. Warm up: what is 5 times 2?
warmUp.why: 5 times 2 is 5 twos, which is 10. Today you will use arrays and times tables.

lessons.title: Equal Parts
lessons.materials: Paper strips to fold into halves, quarters and fifths, and about 10 sweets or beans to share equally. Folding a strip yourself is what makes a fraction a real equal part rather than a shaded picture.
lessons.atHome: Fold paper strips into halves, quarters and fifths and compare the pieces. Share 10 sweets equally among 5 people and say what fraction of the sweets each person gets.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you used times tables. Warm up: a pizza is cut into 4 equal slices. What is one slice called?
warmUp.why: 4 equal parts are quarters. Today you will find many kinds of equal parts.

lessons.title: Shapes and Symmetry
lessons.materials: A small mirror, paper shapes to fold and scissors, and a ruler marked in centimetres. Folding a shape to find its line of symmetry, and measuring right round its edge, are both things a hand does better than a tap.
lessons.atHome: Look for shapes with a line of symmetry around the house, and check by folding a paper copy. Measure all the way round the edge of a book with a ruler to find its perimeter.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you found equal parts. Warm up: how many sides does a hexagon have?
warmUp.why: A hexagon has 6 sides. Today you will name shapes, find lines of symmetry and measure round the edge.

lessons.title: Measure It
lessons.materials: Kitchen scales, a measuring jug, a ruler marked in centimetres, and a right angle to check against - the corner of a book works. Guessing a measurement before checking it on a real scale is the whole point of this lesson.
lessons.atHome: Weigh some fruit on a kitchen scale, read the level in a measuring jug, and guess a length before measuring it in centimetres. Find a corner that is a right angle, then angles that are smaller and bigger than it.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you looked at shapes and perimeter. Warm up: which unit would you use to measure a pencil?
warmUp.why: A pencil is a length, so it is measured in centimetres. Today you will measure length, mass and capacity.

lessons.title: Time and Direction
lessons.materials: A clock with hands, or one drawn on paper with a split pin, and room to stand and point in four directions. Turning the hands yourself, and turning your own body to face north, south, east and west, is how both stick.
lessons.atHome: Read the clock at breakfast and at bedtime, and work out how long something took, such as a meal. Stand in a room and point north, south, east and west, then give directions using those words.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you measured things. Warm up: how many minutes are there in one hour?
warmUp.why: An hour is 60 minutes. Today you will tell the time, read timetables and use north, south, east and west.

lessons.title: Ask, Count and Chart
lessons.materials: Paper for a tally and a bar chart, and a real question to ask everyone at home. A tally a child makes from real answers is worth more than one already drawn for them.
lessons.atHome: Ask everyone at home one question and record the answers in a tally chart, then draw a bar chart together. Talk about things that will happen tomorrow, things that might happen, and things that will not.

warmUp.q: Last lesson, you told the time and followed directions. Warm up: a tally shows one bundle of five and 2 more marks. How many is that?
warmUp.why: A bundle is 5, and 2 more make 7. Today you will ask questions, count and draw charts.

_explorationStepsComment: Teaching steps with no right answer, so check-judging.py does not count them as failures: manipulatives a child explores rather than answers. An entry that stops firing fails the gate - it means the step now judges, or is gone.
